chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah al-Barqi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his father, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Hamzah ibn al-Tayyar, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said to me: 'Write down what I dictate to you: That among our beliefs is that Allah, the Mighty and High, will present proof against the servants based on what He granted them and what He made known to them. Then He sent a Messenger to them, and revealed to him the Book, commanding in it and forbidding. He commanded in it the prayer and the fasting,'

then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) slept in and missed the prayer (1). So He said: 'I make you sleep, and I wake you up. Go and pray, so that they may learn what to do when this happens to them. It is not as they say: 'If one sleeps in and misses it, he is lost.' The same applies to fasting. I make you ill and I cure you. When I cure you, make up for it up.'

Then Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'And so, when you look at all matters, you will not find anyone in hardship (of religion), nor will you find anyone except that Allah has presented proof against him and has will regarding him. And I do not say: They do whatever they wish.'

Then he said: 'Verily, Allah guides and misleads.' And He said: 'They were commanded only according to their capacity.' Whatever Allah commanded people to do, they have the ability to do it. And whatever they do not have the ability to do, it is lifted from them. But most people are devoid of good.'

Then he said: '(No blame is upon the weak nor upon the sick nor upon those who do not find what they should spend to stay being), so long as they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger; that is the way of the doers of good; * Nor upon those who when they came to you that you might carry them.' [The verse] He lifted from them because they do not find (the means).

The Compiler of this book (may Allah be pleased with him) said: His (peace be upon him) word: 'Verily, Allah guides and misleads' means that He, the Mighty and High, guides the believers on the Day of Judgment to Paradise, and misleads the unjust away from Paradise. Verily, the Mighty and High has said: (1) 'Surely (as for) those who believe and do good, their Lord will guide them by their faith; there shall flow from beneath them rivers in gardens of bliss.' (2) And the Mighty and High has said: (3) 'And Allah causes the unjust to go astray.'
ai.seo_question: How does Shia theology explain divine command and human capacity regarding prayer and fasting?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the principle of *al-hujjah* (divine proof), asserting that Allah holds servants accountable only for what they are capable of, thereby lifting obligations like prayer and fasting during sleep or illness until recovery. This narration underscores the Shia theological stance that divine command is proportional to human capacity (*bi-qadr tus'atihim*), ensuring justice in judgment. The compiler further clarifies that 'guidance' and 'misguidance' in the Hereafter are the ultimate consequences of one's earthly actions, rather than arbitrary divine decrees.
